unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The Bloch-Floquet analogy is explicitly imperfect and no actual extension domain or spectral theorem is supplied.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: The L-series equation is straightforward but character and extension claims remain speculative prose.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Sign identification and dilation symmetry offer hints but not a boundary condition
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Identifying X with -X halves the complex XP period to the desired iπ, while continuous dilation symmetry makes time evolution logarithmic; restricting to integer dilations can insert zeta into a superposition but neither forces its vanishing nor forms a group.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Canonical position-momentum exchange yields an almost-correct zero condition
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Proposes closing XP motion by reinjecting asymptotic position flow through momentum, derives an XP-preserving exchange and a functional-equation identity, then exposes a decisive sign mismatch that prevents it from generating the zeros.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: XP naturally realizes dilation, uniform instability, broken time reversal, critical-line power laws, functional-equation phase, and the mean count after regularization, but every attempted compactification leaves missing boundedness, prime-orbit generation, anomalous phases, or a sign-correct zero condition.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The proposal is explicitly speculative and formally Hermitian only; no self-adjoint discrete realization with the Riemann zeros is obtained.

before.text:
positions X that are related by dilations in the group of integers under multiplication
(mod k). An analogy is with the quantum mechanics of a particle in a periodic
potential (e.g., an electron in a crystal): from the Bloch-Floquet theorem, solutions
of the underlying differential equation are all periodic up to a phase factor exp(iα);
each choice of α is a different self-adjoint extension, and generates a discrete spectrum.
The analogy is imperfect, because α is continuous, whereas the L-functions cannot be
continuously parameterized. A closer analogy is with quantization on a torus phase
space [69], where for topological reasons the permited phases are discrete.

after.text:
We can sum up these scattered remarks about XP by returning to the properties
listed at the beginning of this section. XP is consistent with point a, part of b (XP
dynamics is unstable but not bounded), and c, d, g, h, i, and j. Concerning point e,
the appearance of times that are logarithms of integers begins to be plausible in view
of the association between dilation and evolution, but primes do not appear in any
obvious way. We have no explanation of property f.
